clue.text: He'll put on one, having many a problem

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
M, the Roman numeral for a thousand, stands for many
a poser is a puzzling problem

explanation.surface: Someone takes on a burden while wrestling with a great many difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He'll put on' defines someone who imposes, as in putting a burden on others.
explanation.definitionFit: To impose is to put something on someone, so the one doing it is the person who puts it on.

clue.text: Laid on thick by the painter

definitions.text: Laid on thick by the painter

parts.words: Laid on thick by the painter
parts.note: describes paint applied heavily so brush strokes stand out from the canvas

explanation.definitionFit: Impasto is the technique of applying paint in thick layers to a canvas.

clue.text: Game MP rating a free trip

indicators.note: a free trip lets the letters of MP rating a wander loose into a new order

explanation.surface: A politician gets a holiday at no cost and judges it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free trip' rearranges MP RATING A; game here means birds hunted for sport.
explanation.definitionFit: The ptarmigan is a grouse shot for sport, so it is game.

clue.text: Charming words put into letters

explanation.surface: A magic incantation is written out letter by letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A spell is an incantation of magic words; and to spell a word is to write out its letters.

clue.text: Family accounts

explanation.surface: Records of a household's money.
explanation.definitionFit: Relations are relatives or kin; and relations are also narrations or reports of events.

clue.text: Adds extra point to the sauce

indicators.note: an extra item is one slipped in beyond the original, so a letter is added into the sauce

parts.note: catsup is the American spelling of ketchup, a tomato sauce
S, south, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A cook puts one more finishing touch to the sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: CATSUP is the American spelling of ketchup; 'Adds' looks like it governs the sauce but is the definition, in the old sense of casting up a column of figures.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast up is an old phrase for totting up figures, so it means to total or add.

clue.text: Plant with a single name

parts.note: cum is Latin for with, as in a bedroom-cum-study
I, the Roman numeral one, is a single

explanation.surface: A flower whose label carries only one name.
explanation.definitionFit: Cumin is an aromatic herb grown for its seeds, so it is a plant.

clue.text: Check all news to broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters of all news to are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A newsroom editor verifies every story before it goes on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges ALL NEWS TO.
explanation.definitionFit: To stonewall is to block or obstruct, so it means to check progress.

clue.text: Boy standing up super girl

parts.note: a son is a boy

indicators.note: in a down clue standing up means read from the bottom, so the word for super is turned

parts.note: A1 means first-class or super, written AI

explanation.surface: A lad rises to his feet beside an excellent young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (first-class) is written AI in crosswords; 'standing up' suits a down clue, where reading upward turns the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonia is a girl's name, so the word girl stands for it.

clue.text: Indicate there's some wine to finish off

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
to end something is to finish it off

explanation.surface: A host hints there is fortified wine to round off the meal.
explanation.definitionFit: To portend is to signal or foreshadow what is coming, so to indicate it.

clue.text: Set speed the inexperienced driver must keep within

indicators.note: the speed word has to hold the driver's letter inside itself

parts.note: pace is speed, as in a fast pace
L is the learner driver, from the L-plate shown on the car in Britain

explanation.surface: A rule fixes the speed a learner must keep under.
explanation.walkthrough: British learner drivers display an L-plate, so L stands for a learner.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something down is to place it, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: The Parisienne upset poor men as a satirist

parts.note: la is the French feminine word for 'the', the article a Parisian woman would use

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters of poor men are rearranged

explanation.surface: A French woman mocks poor men, and her barbs upset them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Parisienne' points to French, where the feminine article is la.
explanation.definitionFit: A lampooner writes ridicule of people, which is the work of a satirist.

clue.text: Not involved — not backing the fool

parts.note: something simple is uncomplicated, not involved

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the word not is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone keeps out of things and refuses to support the idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not involved' looks like a definition of the whole answer, but it only supplies the first part, simple meaning uncomplicated.
explanation.definitionFit: A simpleton is a foolish, gullible person, a classic synonym for a fool.

clue.text: Remove "Times" editorial for a start

parts.note: eras are periods or times

indicators.note: for a start means take only the opening letter of the word editorial

explanation.surface: An instruction to strike out the Times newspaper's leading article first.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks around "Times" suggest the newspaper; it simply means periods, ERAS.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase something is to wipe it out, so it means to remove.

clue.text: Anything in a trough tempts pigs

indicators.note: in signals that the answer sits within the letters of a trough tempts

explanation.surface: Whatever lands in a feeding trough is a temptation to pigs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pigs' just completes the farmyard picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Ought is an old variant spelling of aught, meaning anything at all.

clue.text: Green tea's brewed specially for young people

indicators.note: brewing mixes things up, so the letters of green tea's are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A café makes green tea particularly for a youthful crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brewed specially' rearranges GREEN TEAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Teenagers are adolescents in their teens, so youngsters.

clue.text: Having a single manual worker take heed and no mistake!

indicators.note: a mistake is a muddle, so the letters of heed and no are jumbled

explanation.surface: An exclamation urging someone with just one labourer to pay attention and avoid errors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistake' rearranges HEED AND NO; the definition reads hand as a manual worker, while 'take' and 'no' dress the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand is a manual worker, so having a single one is having one hand.

clue.text: The look-out man appears uncommonly green

parts.note: extra means unusually or uncommonly, as in extra large
vert is the heraldic word for green, from French

explanation.surface: A sentry on watch looks unusually pale and sickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'look-out' suggests a sentry, but means someone whose attention is turned outwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An extravert is outgoing, interested in the world outside, so a man who looks outward.

clue.text: Depressed Conservatives will be unequivocal

parts.note: down means low in spirits, depressed
the political right is the conservative side

explanation.surface: Gloomy Tories will speak bluntly.
explanation.definitionFit: Downright means utter or plain-spoken, leaving no doubt, so it is unequivocal.

clue.text: Service for those wanting a late meal

definitions.text: Service for those wanting a late meal

parts.words: Service for those wanting a late meal
parts.note: service here means a full set of crockery, the plates and dishes laid for an evening meal

explanation.definitionFit: A service is a matching set of crockery, and the one used for an evening meal is named after that meal.

clue.text: It goes a long way down river, the start of the Pacific Ocean

definitions.text: It goes a long way down

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales

indicators.note: the start of means the opening letter of the word Pacific

parts.note: sea and ocean are synonyms

explanation.surface: A river flows a great distance to reach the Pacific.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes something reaching far below, as deep-sea fishing does.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep-sea describes the ocean's greatest depths, which extend far beneath the surface.

clue.text: Left livestock in the South of England

parts.note: ewes are female sheep, farm livestock

explanation.surface: Sheep left out to graze in southern English fields.
explanation.walkthrough: LEWES is the county town of East Sussex, in the south of England; the definition names its location.
explanation.definitionFit: The town is the county town of East Sussex, on England's south coast, so it is a place in the south.

clue.text: "My ___ for a palmer's walking staff" (Richard II)

definitions.text: "My ___ for a palmer's walking staff" (Richard II)

parts.words: "My ___ for a palmer's walking staff" (Richard II)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank from King Richard's lament, trading the royal rod of office for a pilgrim's stick

explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's Richard II the deposed king offers to swap his royal trappings for a pilgrim's humble gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard trades the ornamental rod a monarch holds, his symbol of authority, for a pilgrim's staff.

clue.text: Before noon she should be in the States

indicators.note: the woman's name belongs inside the country name, so the morning letters are dropped from it

parts.note: America is a common name for the United States
AM, ante meridiem, means before noon

explanation.surface: A woman ought to be in America by the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should be in' reads as the morning letters joining the woman's name to make the country, so removing them from the country leaves her.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is a woman's name, so a female pronoun can stand for it.

clue.text: Not fitting into a drill

parts.note: into gives in
PT, physical training, is drill or exercise

explanation.surface: A recruit who does not suit the army's exercise regime.
explanation.walkthrough: PT, physical training, is the British school and army term for drill.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means unsuitable or inappropriate, so not fitting.

clue.text: Presumption water will be provided by a restaurant

parts.note: brass means cheek or nerve, a bold presumption
Erie is one of the Great Lakes, a body of water

explanation.surface: A diner's nerve in expecting free tap water from a café.
explanation.walkthrough: BRASS (as in brass neck) is British slang for impudence.
explanation.definitionFit: A brasserie is an informal French-style eating place, so it is a kind of restaurant.

clue.text: Man about town told to carry cash

indicators.note: the word for told holds the cash letter inside it, as if carrying it

parts.note: bade is past tense of bid, so ordered or told
L stands for the pound, Latin libra, so money

explanation.surface: A city gent was instructed to bring money with him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to carry' puts L inside BADE, after the B; a blade is an old word for a dashing young man.
explanation.definitionFit: A blade is a dashing, fashionable young man, the old sense of a man about town.

clue.text: Opposed to going in alone to explain

indicators.note: the opposing letter goes into the word for alone

parts.note: sole means single or alone
V, short for versus, means opposed to

explanation.surface: A loner reluctantly joins in to clarify matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going in' places V inside SOLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To solve a mystery is to work it out and make it clear, so to explain it.

clue.text: The jaded fellow sees no advantage either way

parts.note: stale means jaded or tired out
a mate is a companion or fellow

explanation.surface: A weary man finds neither side gaining any ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess term covers any deadlock where neither side gains.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalemate is a deadlock in which neither party can win, so neither side has the edge.

clue.text: The answer to a clue that's humorous

explanation.surface: Someone explains what a crossword solution is and finds it funny.
explanation.definitionFit: Each crossword solution is traditionally called a light; and light verse or comedy is humorous, not serious.

clue.text: This entertainer is a drawer, note

parts.note: an artist draws pictures, so is a drawer
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A performer who also sketches pictures, as one should note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawer' looks like furniture; it means someone who draws.
explanation.definitionFit: An artiste is a professional performer, such as a singer or dancer, so an entertainer.

clue.text: A supporter of the board

parts.note: reads like a backer of a company's directors, but means a frame literally holding up a table top

explanation.definitionFit: A trestle is a frame of legs that holds up a tabletop, so it bears a plank or board.
